title: Unfold a laptop stand and set its highest position
instruction: Fully spread the laptop stand, with both support rods seated in the slots for its highest setting. The whole stand's top-down outline must lie within the inner edges of the red tape rectangle. Leave both base rails resting on the tabletop, release the stand and move both grippers clear.
context: Setting up a portable laptop stand requires coordinated manipulation of a passive scissor linkage, raising two supports, and seating separate support rods. The task tests whether a robot can assemble a stable configuration of a familiar adjustable object.
setup: Two YAM arms, 0.61 m apart, face a 1.1 x 1.3 m oak worktop with top and wrist cameras. Reference: Tonmom stand, Amazon ASIN B08G84P8ZX (purchase link in README). The ABS/silicone model is 0.24 kg, 276 x 53 x 28 mm folded, 185 mm wide open. Start folded, centered at (0.46,0) m, long axis along X, hooks toward -X. A 12 mm red tape border encloses x=[0.29,0.63], y=[-0.12,0.12] m at its inner edges. Seven slots; slot 1 nearest the front hinge is highest. No laptop.
scoring: Score only the final state; lifting, tilting or shaking the stand to unfold it is allowed, with no continuous tabletop-contact requirement. +0.25 for full spread: use a ruler perpendicular to the two parallel support rails to measure between their outer side edges; width >=18 cm (inner gap >=13 cm for the 2.5 cm rails). Below 18 cm earns 0 for this item. +0.25 for each rod seated inside its highest slot (slot 1 nearest the front hinge), not on the rim. These three items score independently. With all three met, add +0.25 if the entire top-down outline is inside the tape inner edges, both base rails rest on the tabletop, and both grippers are released and clear; touching the inner edge is allowed. Use final overhead and side views after release to check containment, both rods seated and the stand resting on both bases without robot support.
run_limit: 2400 control steps at 20 Hz (120 simulated seconds), including 32 Dream history warmup steps. Dream ends early on full success. The scripted demo completes within the same limit.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX model with 10 bodies, 11 passive joints and 114 convex colliders; CPU TGS at 960 Hz. Passive hinges, slides and rod-slot contacts govern the mechanism. Dimensions, mass, inertia and friction use model estimates. Hinge friction is 0.002/0.0004 N m; slide friction is 0.15 N. Pads use rigid collision geometry. PhysX contact reports verify robot release and support at both bases. The expert plans from mechanism state; Dream receives RGB and joint state.
scores: Dream-1 with the submitted instruction and rubric (2026-11-16 UTC): 0.0/1.0 after 2400 steps, 120 s. Robot demo: 1.0/1.0 at 105.05 s; full action replay verified release and tabletop support. Fixed layout, seed 0.
reset_notes: Restore the folded stand to the red rectangle center, long axis along X and hooks toward -X. Reset both arms to their ready pose and reset elapsed time and score. Settle under gravity for 0.5 s. No consumables or randomized placement.
